_: A typical comb plastic, taken as polyamide 6,6 (nylon: moulded combs, brush pins and bristles; matching the hair-comb pair values in pairs/eye_hair.json, measured on polyamide), at 23 C / 50 % RH (conditioned, ~2 % water). States switch it to cellulose acetate (sawn-and-polished premium combs), ABS and polypropylene (cheap moulded combs) and hard rubber (ebonite). The triboelectric position is what decides hair static: nylon sits close to hair and charges it little; PP and hard rubber charge it strongly. Partners research lane 11-07 (PARTNERS.md).

alpha.src: injection-moulded gloss Ra ~0.05-0.2 um; hand-polished acetate smoother; tooth flanks of cheap moulded combs carry a parting-line seam that snags hair

n.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read: nylon 6,6 nD ~1.53 (1.53-1.565 with crystallinity)

n_d.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read, for PA66, ABS and PP; CA n20/D 1.475 (ChemicalBook) and Goodfellow 1.49 from CA_DS

translucency.v: natural PA66 is milky-translucent (crystallite scattering, ~1-3 mm visible depth); acetate is clear and carries deep marbled dyes (tortoiseshell); ABS opaque; PP translucent-waxy

static.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook / ETB, not re-read as a range: nylon on steel 0.3-0.5 static; ETB re-read 11-08 lists nylon on steel 0.4 (clean, dry) and nylon on nylon 0.15-0.25, inside or near the band; against hair fibres 0.17 dry (pairs/eye_hair.json)

kinetic.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read: POLYHB nylon on steel kinetic 0.25-0.4 (rises when it absorbs water and softens)

friction.counterface: polished steel; hair in pairs/eye_hair.json (DEWRI25 polyamide capstan 0.13 dry, 0.25 wet); skin in pairs/partners.json

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: E: recalled from Wu 1982 (WU82) and the Accu Dyne table (ACCUDYNE), not re-read (the Accu Dyne page refused the fetch, 403, 11-08): nylon 6,6 ~46, PP 29-30, ABS ~38-42, cellulose acetate ~42-46

restitution.src: semi-crystalline nylon parts bounce moderately; not measured for combs

collision_thickness_mm.src: numerical offset: comb teeth are 0.6-1.5 mm thick with 0.3-0.5 mm round tips; 0.05 mm keeps the tooth gap (0.5-2 mm) true for hair fibres of 50-100 um diameter

E_star_GPa.src: E / (1 - nu^2) from E 2.8 GPa, nu 0.39 (half-space modulus; the soft partner's own E* combines in series)

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: flat punch k = 2 E* a over area pi a^2, a 50 mm (hand-sized patch): an unyielding barrier next to any soft partner

hertz_constant_N_per_m1_5_R25mm.src: F = (4/3) E* sqrt(R) d^1.5, rigid sphere R 25 mm

contact_damping_ratio.src: zeta = -ln e / sqrt(pi^2 + ln^2 e) from restitution 0.7

restitution.src: polymer spheres / parts on rigid flats e ~0.6-0.8 at 1 m/s (semi-crystalline nylon, tan delta ~0.03); not measured for combs

response_time_ms.src: Hertz contact time t = 2.87 (m^2/(R E*^2 v))^0.2, rigid 1 kg sphere, R 25 mm, 1 m/s: sub-millisecond; in a slap or a step the soft partner sets the pulse

damping_ratio.src: as contact_damping_ratio (energy lost per impact, from restitution)

geometry.src: typical moulded comb tooth (fine teeth 0.6 x 1.2 x 15 mm, wide teeth 1.5 x 2 x 30 mm)

EI_Nm2.src: E b h^3 / 12 with E 2.8 GPa, b 1.5 mm, h 1.0 mm

tip_stiffness_N_m.src: 3 EI / L^3 (cantilever), L 20 mm: a snag of a few hundred mN bends a tooth by mm; hair (EI ~1e-11 N m2) bends first

solver._: A comb is a rigid body with flexible teeth: each tooth a cantilever (tooth_bending) meeting hair fibres (pairs/eye_hair.json) and the scalp (pairs/partners.json).

water_contact_angle_deg.src: E: recalled from the Accu Dyne table (ACCUDYNE), not re-read: ACCUDYNE nylon 6,6 ~68, PP ~102 (recalled); CA and ABS E from their surface energies

wetting._: A wet comb holds water between teeth by capillarity (gap ~1 mm, Laplace ~150 Pa) and drags a water film through hair.

water_absorption.src: NYLON_DS SUSTAMID 66 24 h 1 %, saturation 8.5 %; RS PA66 24 h 1.2 %, sat 7 %; Unitika 50 % RH 1.6 %; CA_DS 24 h 2.3 % (MakeItFrom), 1.9-7 % (Goodfellow); ABS / PP POLYHB; ABS / PP E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook, not re-read

v.position: hair +45 vs nylon +30: a nylon comb takes a little negative charge and leaves hair slightly + (little flyaway); ABS (-5) more; PP (-90) and hard rubber (classic series: negative) strongly. Cellulose acetate not in the nC/J table: classic series place acetate on the negative side, but its water uptake (~2 % at 50 % RH) bleeds charge fast, which is why acetate combs are sold as 'anti-static'

triboelectric.src: ALPHALAB nylon (row 'nylon, dry skin') +30, ABS -5, olefins incl. PP -90, hair +45; cellulose acetate and hard rubber not listed (EESEMI: 'acetate, rayon' and 'hard rubber' negative side)

resistivity_ohm_m.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read: POLYHB / datasheet ranges: absorbed water lowers nylon and acetate by 2-3 decades

permittivity_rel.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read: POLYHB

charge_decay_s.src: follows surface resistivity; flyaway hair after PP combing in dry winter air

hardness.src: E: recalled from the PA66 datasheets (NYLON_DS) / the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read

abrasion.v: nylon wears very little (bearing grade); acetate polishes; cheap moulded seams wear smooth; teeth chip in PP/ABS at low temperature

density_kg_m3.src: NYLON_DS PA66 1.14 g/cm3 (ISO 1183); CA 1.28-1.30, ABS 1.04-1.06, PP 0.90-0.91 (POLYHB); the CA, ABS and PP densities are E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook, not re-read

E_GPa.src: NYLON_DS tensile modulus 2.8 GPa (400 ksi, D638), 3.5 GPa (ISO 527 dry); conditioned E from POLYHB; the conditioned E is E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook, not re-read

E_GPa_used.src: dry-ish value used for the solver numbers (combs are thin and dry out in air); conditioned nylon is ~40 % softer

poisson.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read: POLYHB nylon 0.39-0.41

yield_MPa.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read: POLYHB / datasheets

tan_delta_23C.src: semi-crystalline PA66 below its Tg; acetate (plasticised) ~0.05-0.1

Tg_C.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read: POLYHB: water plasticises nylon below room temperature, so a wet nylon comb is softer and grips hair more

strength_tensile_MPa.src: NYLON_DS / CA_DS (MakeItFrom CA 30-37 MPa) / POLYHB; the ABS / PP values E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook, not re-read

toughness.v: PA66 and acetate tough (teeth bend, then whiten); ABS and PP at low temperature snap at the tooth root

conductivity_W_mK.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB) / PA66 datasheets (NYLON_DS), not re-read: PA66 0.23-0.29 W/mK

heat_capacity_J_kgK.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read: PA66 1.67-1.7 J/gK

effusivity.src: sqrt(k rho c) = sqrt(0.25 x 1140 x 1700) W s^0.5 m^-2 K^-1

contact_temp_with_skin_C.src: SKINTH: T = (e_skin 33 + e 20)/(e_skin + e), skin 33 C on material 20 C, e_skin 1188; lower = feels colder

emissivity.src: E: EMIS_ETB re-read 11-08 lists no nylon row; its 'Plastics' row is 0.90-0.97 (PP 0.97, PVC 0.91-0.93); 0.9 kept as E (the src had said 'nylon ~0.9')

wet.src: soaked nylon (water ~8 %) softens (Tg below room temperature); pairs/eye_hair.json carries hair-on-comb wet 0.25

cellulose_acetate.src: CA_DS density 1.3, flexural modulus 1.7-2.1 GPa, n 1.475; sawn and hand-polished premium combs (rounded teeth, no seam); charge leaks via absorbed water

abs.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read: POLYHB ABS 1.04-1.06, E 2.0-2.6 GPa; opaque moulded comb with parting seams; ALPHALAB -5 nC/J

polypropylene.src: E: recalled from the Polymer Handbook (POLYHB), not re-read: POLYHB PP 0.90-0.91, E 1.1-1.6 GPa; ALPHALAB -90 nC/J: the strongly charging comb

hard_rubber_ebonite.src: E: recalled from textbook / trade ranges, not re-read: vulcanite / ebonite (NR + 30-40 % sulphur): density 1.15-1.2, E 2-3 GPa, black gloss; charges hair strongly (the classic 'rubbed comb picks up paper')

humid_RH80.src: surface water film: static on all comb plastics bleeds in seconds; flyaway mostly gone (charge falls linearly 20-50 % RH, LUNN77 in pairs/eye_hair.json)

ETB.cite: The Engineering ToolBox, Friction and friction coefficients for some common materials
ETB.lic: free web reference; numbers used as facts (friction table re-read 11-08)

ALPHALAB.cite: Lee B / AlphaLab Inc. (TriField) triboelectric table, charge affinity nC/J (positive = charges +); zero = the average conductor (all metals about equal); read via the storiesinfabric.blogspot.com reprint 11-07
ALPHALAB.lic: free web table, reproduction only in whole: single numbers used as facts, table not copied STUDY ONLY (P13)

SKINTH.cite: skin thermal inputs for contact temperature: k 0.37 W/mK, c 3500 J/kgK (Duck 1990 tissue tables, typical), rho 1090 from skin.body

DERLER12.cite: Derler S, Gerhardt L-C. Tribology of skin: review and analysis of experimental results for the friction coefficient of human skin. Tribol Lett 45:1-27 (2012)

NYLON_DS.cite: PA66 datasheets: Sustamid 66 (Port Plastics) density 1.14, water 24 h 1 %, saturation 8.5 %; RS PA66 tensile modulus 400 ksi (2.8 GPa), 24 h 1.2 %, sat 7 %; Ensinger TECAMID 66 E 3.5 GPa (ISO 527); Unitika 50 % RH equilibrium 1.6 %
NYLON_DS.lic: manufacturer datasheets; numbers used as facts

CA_DS.cite: Cellulose acetate: MakeItFrom (density 1.3, flexural modulus 1.7-2.1 GPa, UTS 30-37 MPa, water 24 h 2.3 %); Goodfellow (density 1.3, n 1.49, water 1.9-7 %); ChemicalBook n20/D 1.475
CA_DS.lic: copyrighted web compilations / supplier pages: single numbers used as facts STUDY ONLY (P13)

ACCUDYNE.cite: Diversified Enterprises (Accu Dyne Test), Critical surface tension and contact angle with water for various polymers (nylon 6,6 ~46 mJ/m2, water ~68 deg; PP ~30, ~102 deg)
ACCUDYNE.lic: free web table; numbers used as facts (recalled from the source, not re-read 11-07)

EESEMI.cite: EESemi.com triboelectric series (collated qualitative ranking: nylon and human hair positive; acetate/rayon, hard rubber, polypropylene negative)

POLYHB.cite: Brandrup J, Immergut EH, Grulke EA (eds). Polymer Handbook, 4th ed. (Wiley 1999) / Mark JE (ed). Physical Properties of Polymers Handbook: refractive index, surface energy, thermal values of NR, SBR, PA66, CA, ABS, PP

WU82.lic: book; numbers used as facts (recalled from the source, not re-read 11-07)
